frequency_question: How often do observable precursor signals of impending federal revocation of an accrediting body actually proceed to a final revocation order within a two-to-three-year window?
membership_rule: Includes any formal US Department of Education or equivalent federal oversight proceeding targeting a recognized national professional accreditation entity that reaches a final determination of revocation. Excludes voluntary relinquishments, minor probations that do not result in loss of recognition, and non-professional academic bodies.

cases.name: American Bar Association accreditation review challenges and notice cycles
ACICS (Accrediting Council for Independent Colleges and Schools) initial federal recognition withdrawal proceedings
ACICS final termination of recognition by the Department of Education

provenance_note: claims 15 cases from only 3 named (5.0x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 15 major contested review cycles identified in federal recognition history; 2 resulted in terminal revocation.
known_gaps: Excludes minor institutional accreditors whose loss of recognition did not involve prominent professional guilds like law or medicine.
skeleton: Federal recognition review cycles for major national accrediting bodies multiplied by the historical fraction where formal show-cause or limitation notices escalate to complete revocation rather than remediation.
multiplier: 2 major challenged national accrediting entities across 3 decades experiencing terminal revocation proceedings out of roughly 15 major contested oversight reviews = 2/15 base rate for full revocation when formal friction is high.
validity_reason: Federal administrative procedures governing recognized accreditors remain governed by stable statutory frameworks unlikely to overhaul completely within two years.
